topic: Two siblings inherit their grandmother's house
text: Of all the houses in the world, why this one? I walk through the door, and every creak is a whisper of her, reminding me of her in ways I don’t want to remember. The walls are too thick with her presence, the air too heavy with the scent of lavender and mothballs. My sibling, they saunter in like they own the place, already talking about selling it, stripping it of its history. I touch the wallpaper, peeling at the edges, and think of all the time she spent here, alone, while we built our lives elsewhere. I won’t let them reduce this to just another sale, just another transaction. This is more than a house; it’s a vault of memories, and they’re not for auction.
